body:
Found while fixing #1097 (the Discover/Random naming split). With a de-locale user
hitting `/opds` on the running image, the catalog root mixes translated and
untranslated entries:

    <title>Alphabetical Books</title>     <- English
    <title>Recently added Books</title>   <- English
    <title>Entdecken</title>              <- ok (after the #1097 fix)
    <title>Regale</title>                 <- ok
    <title>Magic Shelves</title>          <- English

Measured against the compiled `.mo` inside the container, not the `.po`:

    UNTRANSLATED  'Alphabetical Books'
    UNTRANSLATED  'Recently added Books'
    UNTRANSLATED  'Magic Shelves'
    UNTRANSLATED  'Books organized in magic shelves'
    ok            'Shelves' / 'Hot Books' / 'Top Rated Books' /
                  'Currently Reading' / 'Unread Books'

These are exactly the keys the OPDS_ROOT_ENTRY_DEFS comment calls out as having
been added later (books, recent, magic_shelves). #121 wrapped them in N_() so
pybabel would extract them, which worked — but extraction only puts a msgid in the
catalog, it does not translate it. So they have been empty since, sitting next to
older keys that are translated, which is what makes it read as a bug rather than
as missing coverage.

Deliberately not fixed in the #1097 PR: that change is one line and one msgid, and
this needs a translation pass rather than a code change. Worth checking the other
27 locales before deciding scope — de is the one actually measured here.

Same class as the fuzzy-drop in #1097: 'Random Books' was '#, fuzzy' in de/km/no,
and msgfmt drops fuzzy entries silently.
title: OPDS catalog root still shows four English strings to a German user
